lead: Illinois plumbing deals with cold winters, basements, flooding and a lot of old lead service lines. PipeMend sends licensed local plumbers from Chicago to Springfield.
risk: lead service lines, flooded basements and sewer backups, and frozen pipes
risk_short: lead lines, flooded basements and frozen pipes
why: Chicago has one of the largest numbers of lead service lines in the country, and Illinois law requires utilities to replace them over time. Many older homes also have cast-iron drains and old sewer laterals.

Heavy rain floods basements and backs up sewers, so sump pumps, overhead sewers and backwater valves are common. Winters freeze pipes. The Illinois Department of Public Health licenses plumbers statewide.
tips: Test your sump pump and add a battery backup.
Ask your utility about your service line.
Consider a backwater valve if your basement has flooded.
areas: Calls come from Chicago and its suburbs, Rockford, Peoria, Springfield, Champaign, the Quad Cities and southern Illinois.

faq.q: Does my Chicago home have a lead service line?
faq.a: It might. Chicago has a very large number of lead service lines, especially in older homes. The city has a lookup tool, and a plumber can check the pipe where it enters your basement.
